title: Why Everyone Picks the Same Random Number #shorts

lines.text: Someone asked two hundred thousand people to pick a random number from one to a hundred, and they kept picking the same few numbers.
Picture a guy with a microphone stopping people on the street.
"Quick, random number, one to a hundred." A man thinks really hard and goes, "Thirty seven."
Next lady. "Seventy three." Next guy. "Seventy seven."
His buddy with the clipboard says, "Wow. Super random crowd today."
Meanwhile, almost nobody says ninety, or thirty, or forty.
And if you only ask for one to ten, a huge chunk of people just say seven.
You see, your brain has a picture of what random looks like, and it's really picky.
Even numbers feel too neat. Numbers ending in zero feel planned. One and a hundred are right there in the question.
So it grabs something odd, not too big, not too small, that doesn't mean anything. Like thirty seven.
It's like trying to stand out in a crowd by wearing the weirdest outfit you own.
Then you show up, and everyone else had the exact same idea.
So the most random number people can think of is about the least random number there is.
